title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: 《了不起的盖茨比》是美国爵士时代文学巨匠弗朗西斯·司各特·菲茨杰拉德于 1925 年出版的文学巅峰巨作。故事通过旁观者尼克·卡拉威的视角，讲述了出身贫寒的年轻军官詹姆斯·盖兹为了重新赢回富家女黛西·费伊的爱，改名盖茨比并通过非法手段积聚巨额财富。他在纽约西埃格建造奢华豪宅，每晚举办无名宾客云集的盛大舞会，只为凝视黛西家码头那一抹绿光。然而，当盖茨比终于与黛西重逢，迎来的却是虚无的幻灭、冷酷的背叛与悲剧的枪声，揭示了“美国梦”破灭的深刻悲剧。

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Green Light across the Bay
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 1 章：海湾对岸的绿色光芒

paragraphs.en: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I've been turning over in my mind ever since. 'Whenever you feel like criticizing any one,' he told me, 'just remember that all the people in this world haven't had the advantages that you've had.' In consequence, I'm inclined to reserve all judgments, a habit that has opened up many curious natures to me and also made me the victim of a few veteran bores.
paragraphs.zh: 在我年幼且更为脆弱的岁月里，我父亲给我提供了一些建议，从那以后我一直在脑海中反复回味。“每当你觉得想要批评任何人的时候，”他告诉我，“只要记住，这个世界上不是所有人都有你所拥有的那些优势。”结果，我倾向于保留所有的判断，这一习惯向我展示了许多好奇的天性，也使我成为一些老牌无聊之人的受害者。

paragraphs.en: In the spring of 1922, I came East to London to learn the bond business. I rented a small weather-beaten cardboard bungalow at West Egg, Long Island, surrounded by colossal marble mansions. Right next door to my modest house was a huge, extravagant castle, a colossal imitation of some Hôtel de Ville in Normandy, with a tower on one side and forty acres of lawn and garden. It was the mansion of Mr. Jay Gatsby, a mysterious millionaire whose identity was shrouded in rumors.
paragraphs.zh: 在 1922 年的春天，我来到东部学习债券业务。我在长岛的西埃格租了一栋风吹日晒的小纸板农舍，被庞大的大理石豪宅包围着。就在我谦逊房子隔壁的是一座巨大奢华的城堡（某座诺曼底市政厅的庞大模仿品），一侧带有塔楼，配有四十英灵的草坪与花园。那是杰·盖茨比先生的豪宅，一位身份笼罩在谣言中的神秘百万富翁。

paragraphs.en: Across the dark bay, at fashionable East Egg, lived my wealthy cousin Daisy Fay and her husband, Tom Buchanan, a former college football star with a cruel, arrogant manner and unlimited old money. Visiting their mansion for dinner, I met Jordan Baker, a cool, cynical professional golfer. During dinner, the phone rang, and Jordan whispered to me that Tom was having an affair with a mistress in New York.
paragraphs.zh: 在昏暗的海湾对岸，在时尚的东埃格，住着我富有的表妹黛西·费伊和她的丈夫汤姆·布坎南（一位前大学橄榄球明星，带着残酷傲慢的态度与无尽的老钱）。拜访他们的豪宅吃晚餐，我遇到了乔丹·贝克，一位凉爽讽刺的专业高尔夫球手。在晚餐期间电话响了，乔丹向我低语汤姆在纽约和情妇有外遇。

paragraphs.en: Returning home late that night, I saw Mr. Gatsby standing alone on his dark lawn, looking out toward the dark water. He stretched out his arms toward the dark sea in a curious ways, trembling slightly. Looking out across the black bay, I could distinguish nothing except a single green light, minute and far away, that burned at the end of Daisy's dock.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上很晚回到家，我看到盖茨比先生独自站在他昏暗的草坪上，看向昏暗的水面。他以一种好奇的方式向着昏暗的大海伸出双手，稍微发抖。看向漆黑的海湾对岸，除了在黛西码头末端燃烧着的一抹单薄而遥远的绿色光芒外，我什么也辨认不出。

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Valley of Ashes and Myrtle Wilson
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 2 章：灰烬之谷与茉特尔·威尔逊

paragraphs.en: Halfway between West Egg and New York, the road runs alongside a desolate plain known as the Valley of Ashes. It is a fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens, where ashes take the forms of houses and chimneys and rising smoke. Brooding over this solemn wasteland are the giant, faded blue eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg, painted on an old advertising billboard overlooking the ash heaps.
paragraphs.zh: 在西埃格与纽约半途，道路沿着一片被称为“灰烬之谷”的荒凉平原延伸。那是一个奇幻的农场，灰烬像小麦一样长成垄岗、山丘和怪诞的花园，灰烬在那里采取房屋、烟囱和上升浓烟的形式。在这片庄严的荒地上空，挂着大夫 T·J·埃克尔堡巨型褪色的蓝色双眼，画在一张俯瞰灰烬堆的旧广告牌上。

paragraphs.en: One afternoon, Tom Buchanan forced me to get off the train with him at the Valley of Ashes to meet his mistress, Myrtle Wilson. Myrtle was a plump, sensuous woman married to George Wilson, a lifeless garage mechanic covered in gray ash dust. Tom dragged Myrtle to a secret apartment he rented in Manhattan, where they hosted a wild, drunken afternoon party with her neighbors.
paragraphs.zh: 一天下午，汤姆·布坎南强迫我和他一起在灰烬之谷下火车，去见他的情妇茉特尔·威尔逊。茉特尔是一个丰满感性的女人，嫁给了乔治·威尔逊（一位覆盖着灰色灰尘、毫无生气的车库机械师）。汤姆把茉特尔拖到了他在曼哈顿租的一处秘密公寓，在那里他们和她的邻居举办了一场狂乱酗酒的下午聚会。

paragraphs.en: As the alcohol flowed and the music blared, Myrtle grew increasingly loud and arrogant. She began chanting Daisy's name repeatedly to taunt Tom. Enraged by her defiance, Tom struck her across the face with his open hand, breaking her nose with a single bloody blow. The party dissolved in bloody chaos, and I ended up waiting for the 4:00 AM train at the station.
paragraphs.zh: 随着酒精流动、音乐咆哮，茉特尔变得越来越大声和傲慢。她开始重复念叨着黛西的名字来嘲弄汤姆。被她的反抗所激怒，汤姆用张开的手掌迎面打了她，用单次流血的击打砸断了她的鼻子。聚会在流血的混乱中解散，我最终在车站等待凌晨四点的火车。

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Lavish Parties at West Egg
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：西埃格的奢华舞会与神秘盖茨比

paragraphs.en: There was music from my neighbor's house through the summer nights. In his blue gardens men and girls came and went like moths among the whisperings and the champagne and the stars. At least once a week a corps of caterers came down with several hundred feet of canvas and enough colored lights to make a Christmas tree of Gatsby's enormous garden. Every weekend, hundreds of uninvited guests flooded his estate to drink his alcohol and swim in his marble pool.
paragraphs.zh: 在夏夜里从我邻居的房子里传来音乐。在他蓝色的花园里，男人们和女人们像蛾子一样在低语、香槟与星光中来来往往。每周至少有一次，餐饮团队带着几百英尺的画布和足够的彩色灯光降临，把盖茨比巨大的花园装扮成圣诞树。每个周末，几百个未经邀请的宾客涌入他的庄园喝他的酒、在他的大理石泳池里游泳。

paragraphs.en: I was one of the few guests who had actually received a formal written invitation from Gatsby. Attending the party, I searched for the host, but no one knew what he looked like. Wild rumors circulated among the crowd: some claimed Gatsby was a German spy during the war; others insisted he had killed a man in cold blood, or was the nephew of Kaiser Wilhelm.
paragraphs.zh: 我是实际上收到盖茨比正式书面邀请的少数宾客之一。参加聚会，我寻找着主人，但没人知道他长什么样。狂乱的谣言在人群中流传：有人声称盖茨比在战争期间是德国间谍；其他人坚持说他冷血杀过人，或是德皇威廉的侄子。

paragraphs.en: Sitting at a table with Jordan Baker, a handsome man in his early thirties smiled warmly at me and remarked, 'Your face is familiar. Weren't you in the First Division during the war?' We chatted easily about hydroplanes until he introduced himself with a gentle bow: 'I'm Gatsby.' His smile was extraordinary—one of those rare smiles with a quality of eternal reassurance that you may come across four or five times in life.
paragraphs.zh: 与乔丹·贝克坐在桌旁，一位三十多岁出头的英俊男人对我温和地笑着说：“你的脸很熟悉。你在战争期间不是在一师吗？”我们轻松地聊着水上飞机，直到他带着温柔的鞠躬自我介绍：“我是盖茨比。”他的微笑是非凡的（那种带着永恒安慰特质的罕见微笑之一，你在生命中可能会遇到四或五次）。

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Secrets of Jay Gatsby
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：盖茨比的神秘往事与豪车

paragraphs.en: One July morning, Gatsby drove his gorgeous cream-colored Duesenberg motor car up to my cottage and invited me to lunch in New York. As we sped across the Queensboro Bridge, Gatsby began telling me his background, claiming he was the son of wealthy dead parents from San Francisco, educated at Oxford, and decorated for bravery in World War I. Seeing my skepticism, he produced an authentic medal from Montenegro and a photograph of himself at Oxford.
paragraphs.zh: 在七月的一个早上，盖茨比开着他华丽的奶油色杜森贝格汽车来到我的农舍，邀请我在纽约吃午餐。当飞快越过皇后区大桥时，盖茨比开始告诉我他的背景，声称他是旧金山富有已故父母的儿子，在牛津接受教育，并在第一次世界大战中因勇敢获得勋章。看到我的怀疑，他出示了一枚来自黑山的真实勋章和他自己在牛津的照片。

paragraphs.en: In New York, Gatsby introduced me to Meyer Wolfsheim, a shady gangster with cuff buttons made of human molars, who had fixed the 1919 World Series. Later, Jordan Baker revealed the true secret to me: Five years earlier, in Louisville, young army officer Gatsby had fallen deeply in love with rich socialite Daisy Fay. But Gatsby was sent off to war, and Daisy married Tom Buchanan for his wealth.
paragraphs.zh: 在纽约，盖茨比把我介绍给了迈尔·沃尔夫沙伊姆，一位袖扣由人类臼齿做成的阴暗帮派分子，他操纵了 1919 年的世界大赛。后来，乔丹·贝克向我揭露了真正的秘密：五年前在路易斯维尔，年轻的军官盖茨比深深爱上了富有的社交名媛黛西·费伊。但盖茨比被派往战场，黛西为了财产嫁给了汤姆·布坎南。

paragraphs.en: Gatsby had bought his West Egg mansion solely because it was directly across the bay from Daisy's house, and held his extravagant parties hoping she might wander in one night. Jordan conveyed Gatsby's humble plea to me: Would I invite Daisy to my cottage for tea, and allow Gatsby to 'incidentally' drop in to meet her?
paragraphs.zh: 盖茨比购买他的西埃格豪宅完全是因为它正对着黛西家海湾对岸，并且举办奢华聚会希望她可能会在某个晚上溜进来。乔丹向我转达了盖茨比谦逊的请求：我能否邀请黛西来我的农舍喝茶，并允许盖茨比“偶然”走进来与她见面？

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Reunion with Daisy Fay
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：雨中重逢与大吉他梦幻

paragraphs.en: On a rainy afternoon, Daisy came to my cottage for tea, unaware of Gatsby's presence. Gatsby, nervous to the point of panic, knocked on my door soaked with rain. When Daisy stepped into the living-room and saw Gatsby standing by the mantelpiece, she froze in shock, her breath catching in her throat.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个下雨的下午，黛西来到我的农舍喝茶，没有意识到盖茨比的存在。盖茨比紧张到了恐慌的地步，敲开我的门时浑身被雨淋透。当黛西步入客厅看到盖茨比站在壁炉旁时，她在震惊中呆立，呼吸停在喉咙里。

paragraphs.en: At first, the embarrassment was painful and agonizing. Leaving them alone for half an hour, I returned to find the awkwardness completely gone. Daisy was weeping tears of joy, and Gatsby was glowing with radiant happiness. The rain had stopped, and Gatsby invited us over to tour his marble palace.
paragraphs.zh: 最初，尴尬是痛苦和折磨人的。把他们留单独待了半个小时，我回来发现尴尬完全消失了。黛西流着喜悦的眼泪，而盖茨比散发着绚丽的幸福。雨停了，盖茨比邀请我们去参观他的大理石城堡。

paragraphs.en: As Gatsby showed Daisy his luxurious rooms, throwing dozens of imported silk shirts onto his bed, Daisy buried her face in the silk and wept bitterly: 'They're such beautiful shirts! It makes me sad because I've never seen such beautiful shirts before.' Looking out across the bay at the green light on her dock, Gatsby realized that the colossal significance of that light was now gone forever, swallowed up by the living reality of Daisy beside him.
paragraphs.zh: 当盖茨比向黛西展示他奢华的房间，把几十件进口丝绸衬衫扔到床上时，黛西把脸埋在丝绸里号啕大哭：“它们是如此美丽的衬衫！这让我伤心，因为我以前从未见过如此美丽的衬衫。”看向海湾对岸她码头上的绿光，盖茨比意识到那抹光芒的巨大意义现在永远消失了，被身旁黛西活生生的现实所吞噬。

chapters.title: Chapter 6: The True Story of James Gatz
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 6 章：詹姆斯·盖兹的真实出身

paragraphs.en: It was during this time that a reporter arrived at Gatsby's door, seeking information about his mysterious past. The true story of Jay Gatsby was far different from his legendary origin: his real name was James Gatz, born to poor, unsuccessful farmers in North Dakota. He had worked as a clam-digger and salmon-fisher on Lake Superior, burning with an intense ambition for wealth and glory.
paragraphs.zh: 正是在这段时间里，一位记者来到盖茨比门口寻求关于他神秘过去的线索。杰·盖茨比真实的故事与他传奇的出身截然不同：他的真名叫詹姆斯·盖兹，出生于北达科他州贫穷不成功的农民家庭。他曾在苏必利尔湖上做过蛤蜊挖掘工和鲑鱼渔夫，燃烧着对财富与荣耀的强烈野心。

paragraphs.en: At seventeen, he rescued Dan Cody, an eccentric copper millionaire, from a storm on Lake Superior. Cody took young Gatz aboard his yacht as his assistant, renaming him Jay Gatsby and teaching him the manners of the wealthy elite. For five years, Gatsby traveled the world on Cody's yacht, learning to abstain from heavy drinking and cultivating his aristocratic poise.
paragraphs.zh: 十七岁时，他在苏必利尔湖的暴风雨中拯救了丹·柯迪（一位古怪的铜业百万富翁）。柯迪带着年轻的盖兹登上他的游艇作为助手，把他改名为杰·盖茨比，并教他富有精英的举止。五年里，盖茨比在柯迪的游艇上环游世界，学会了节制酗酒并培养了他的贵族姿态。

paragraphs.en: Soon after, Tom Buchanan accompanied Daisy to one of Gatsby's Saturday night parties. Tom was suspicious and arrogant, looking down on the 'nouveau riche' West Egg crowds. Daisy was appalled by the raw, vulgar atmosphere of the party. After they left, Gatsby confessed his deep despair to me: he wanted Daisy to leave Tom and erase the past five years, recreating their pure love as if time had stood still.
paragraphs.zh: 不久之后，汤姆·布坎南陪同黛西参加了盖茨比周六晚上的一次聚会。汤姆充满怀疑且傲慢，看不起西德尼的新富人群。黛西被聚会原始粗俗的氛围所震惊。他们离开后，盖茨比向我吐露了他深沉的绝望：他要黛西离开汤姆并抹去过去的五年，重新创造他们纯洁的爱仿佛时光倒流。

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Plaza Hotel Conflict and the Fatal Crash
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：广场酒店摊牌与致命车祸

paragraphs.en: On the hottest day of the summer, Daisy invited Gatsby, Jordan, and me to her mansion. With Tom in the next room, Daisy kissed Gatsby on the lips, confessing her love. Sensing the affair, a furious Tom insisted they all drive to New York. Tom drove Gatsby's yellow Duesenberg with Jordan and me, while Gatsby drove Tom's blue coupe with Daisy.
paragraphs.zh: 在夏天最热的一天，黛西邀请盖茨比、乔丹和我去她的豪宅。隔壁房间有汤姆，黛西亲吻了盖茨比的双唇，承认了她的爱。察觉到外遇，愤怒的汤姆坚持他们全部开车去纽约。汤姆开着盖茨比黄色的杜森贝格带着乔丹和我，而盖茨比开着汤姆蓝色的双门轿车带着黛西。

paragraphs.en: At a suite in the Plaza Hotel, the stifling heat exploded into confrontation. Tom savagely attacked Gatsby's shady bootlegging business and demanded to know his intentions. Gatsby stood tall, declaring: 'Your wife doesn't love you! She's never loved you. She loves me!' But when Tom forced Daisy to speak, Daisy broke down in tears, confessing: 'I did love him once—but I loved you too.'
paragraphs.zh: 在广场酒店的一间套房里，窒息的热浪爆发出对抗。汤姆野蛮地攻击盖茨比阴暗的私酒生意，并要求知道他的意图。盖茨比挺直身姿宣布：“你的妻子不爱你！她从未爱过你。她爱我！”但当汤姆强迫黛西说话时，黛西在眼泪中崩溃，承认：“我曾经爱过他——但也爱过你。”

paragraphs.en: Realizing Gatsby had lost, a triumphant Tom sent Daisy home with Gatsby in the yellow car. Returning through the Valley of Ashes, we arrived at a horrific accident scene: Myrtle Wilson had been struck and killed by a speeding yellow car that fled into the dark night! George Wilson was weeping uncontrollably, screaming for vengeance against the yellow car's driver.
paragraphs.zh: 意识到盖茨比输了，胜利的汤姆让黛西与盖茨比坐黄色车回家。返回穿过灰烬之谷，我们到达了一个可怕的事故现场：茉特尔·威尔逊被一辆超速行驶、逃入黑夜的黄色车撞死！乔治·威尔逊无控地哭泣，尖叫着要向黄色车的司机复仇。

paragraphs.en: That night, outside Daisy's mansion, I found Gatsby hiding in the bushes to protect Daisy. Gatsby revealed the heartbreaking truth to me: Daisy had been driving the yellow car when Myrtle rushed into the street, but Gatsby vowed to take the blame himself to protect his beloved Daisy.
paragraphs.zh: 那天 night，在黛西豪宅外，我发现盖茨比藏在灌木丛里保护黛西。盖茨比向我揭露了令人心碎的真相：当茉特尔冲进街道时是黛西在开黄色车，但盖茨比发誓要自己承担责任来保护他亲爱的黛西。

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Tragedy and the Vanishing American Dream
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：悲剧终局与消逝的美国梦

paragraphs.en: The next morning, I visited Gatsby at his quiet mansion. I urged him to leave West Egg and go away before the police traced his yellow car, but he refused to leave while Daisy might need him. That afternoon, Gatsby decided to swim in his marble pool for the first time all summer, waiting by the telephone for a call from Daisy that would never come.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，我在盖茨比安静的豪宅拜访了他。我敦促他在警察追踪到他的黄车前离开西埃格远走高飞，但他拒绝离开，因为黛西可能需要他。那天下午，盖茨比决定整个夏天第一次在他的大理石泳池里游泳，在电话旁等待着黛西永远不会打来的电话。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Tom Buchanan had told the grieving George Wilson that the yellow car belonged to Jay Gatsby. Consumed by mad vengeance, Wilson tracked Gatsby to his estate. As Gatsby floated peacefully on an air mattress in his pool, Wilson shot him dead, then turned the gun on himself in the bushes.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，汤姆·布坎南告诉悲伤的乔治·威尔逊那辆黄色车属于杰·盖茨比。被疯狂的复仇所吞噬，威尔逊在盖茨比的庄园追踪到了他。当盖茨比平静地漂浮在泳池的气垫上时，威尔逊将他枪杀，然后在灌木丛里开枪自尽。

paragraphs.en: I arranged Gatsby's funeral, but to my bitterness, not a single one of his hundreds of party guests came to pay their respects. Daisy and Tom had left town without leaving an address. Only Gatsby's elderly father, Henry Gatz, and a single guest attended the burial in the rain.
paragraphs.zh: 我安排了盖茨比的葬礼，但令我痛苦的是，他几百个聚会宾客中没有一个人来表达敬意。黛西和汤姆离开小镇没有留下地址。只有盖茨比年老的父亲亨利·盖兹和一位单独的宾客参加了雨中的葬礼。

paragraphs.en: Disgusted by the cold, careless materialism of the East, I decided to return home to the Midwest. On my last night, I walked down to the shore and stood on Gatsby's beach. I thought of Gatsby's wonder when he first picked out the green light at the end of Daisy's dock. He had come a long way to this blue lawn, and his dream must have seemed so close that he could hardly fail to grasp it. He did not know that it was already behind him.
paragraphs.zh: 被东部冰冷粗心的物质主义所恶心，我决定回家去中西部。在我最后一个晚上，我走下海岸站在盖茨比的沙滩上。我想起了盖茨比最初挑选出黛西码头末端绿光时的奇迹。他走过了漫长的道路来到这片蓝色的草坪，他的梦想一定显得如此接近以至于他几乎不可能抓不住它。他不知道它已经在他身后了。

paragraphs.en: Gatsby believed in the green light, the orgastic future that year by year recedes before us. It eluded us then, but that's no matter—tomorrow we will run faster, stretch out our arms farther... And one fine morning—So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
paragraphs.zh: 盖茨比相信那抹绿光，相信年复一年在我们面前消退的高潮般的未来。它当时避开了我们，但那没有关系——明天我们会跑得更快，手臂伸得更远……在某个晴朗的早上——于是我们奋力前行，逆水行舟，不停地被浪潮推回到过去。
